stories.title: Alcaraz Beats Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 — Qualifies as Lendl Group Winner

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Carlos Alcaraz beats Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 to book his ATP Finals semifinal spot. Zero break points conceded. 11-match winning streak. H2H with Medvedev now 8-3. He's through. #ATPFinals #Tennis #ATP #Alcaraz

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Alcaraz had his left thigh strapped and needed a medical timeout against Medvedev. Still won 6-2, 6-4 without conceding a break point. That is a 11-match winning streak through an injury scare. #ATPFinals #Tennis #ATP #Alcaraz

facebook.long_form:
Carlos Alcaraz is in the ATP Finals semifinals, and he got there in emphatic fashion.

He beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 on Wednesday in Turin — finishing in roughly 72 minutes, conceding zero break points, and extending his winning streak to 11 matches. The head-to-head record against Medvedev is now 8-3 in Alcaraz's favour.

There was one moment of concern. Alcaraz took a medical timeout for his left thigh mid-match, emerging with the leg visibly strapped. It slowed nothing down. He closed out the second set without drama and confirmed his place in the last four as the Ivan Lendl Group winner.

Medvedev is now 1-1 and must beat Frances Tiafoe on Friday to advance. For Alcaraz, the semifinal awaits — and given the form he is in, whoever comes out of the McEnroe Group will have their work cut out.

Who do you think Alcaraz will face in the semifinals?

stories.title: Tiafoe Beats Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0 — First ATP Finals Win

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: Frances Tiafoe was down two set points in the tiebreak. Saved them, won it 8-6. Then won the second set 6-0. His first ever ATP Finals win, against Cobolli. 92 minutes of work. #ATPFinals #Tennis #ATP #Tiafoe

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Cobolli exits the ATP Finals without a win, 0-2 in the Lendl Group. Played in front of his home crowd in Turin and lost both matches. That is tough. Tiafoe is now 1-1 and plays Medvedev Friday. #ATPFinals #Tennis #ATP #Cobolli

facebook.long_form:
Frances Tiafoe has been to the ATP Finals before. He never won a match there — until Wednesday.

He beat Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0 in Turin, and the story of the match was written in the first-set tiebreak. Cobolli led 6-4, holding two set points. Tiafoe saved them both, then won the tiebreak 8-6. After that, the second set was one-sided: 6-0, with Tiafoe winning every game.

It was a tough night for Cobolli. He was playing in his home country, in front of a Turin crowd that wanted him to do well. He finishes the group stage 0-2, without a win, having led in the tiebreak of his second match and still come up short.

Tiafoe is now 1-1. He plays Daniil Medvedev on Friday for a place in the semifinals.

What do you think of Tiafoe's chances against Medvedev?

stories.title: ATP Finals Day 5 — Shelton vs Jodar and Fils vs Zverev Decide the McEnroe Group

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: ATP Finals Day 5 — McEnroe Group finale. Shelton (1-1) vs Jodar (0-2) not before 2pm CET. Fils (1-1) vs Zverev (2-0) not before 8:30pm CET. Shelton wins: he is through. If not, Fils's fate depends on the standings. #ATPFinals #Tennis #ATP #ATPFinals2026

facebook.long_form:
The McEnroe Group finale is today, and two players have something significant at stake.

Ben Shelton (1-1) plays Rafael Jodar (0-2) this afternoon — not before 2:00 PM CET. Shelton needs the win to book his place in the ATP Finals semifinals. Jodar is already eliminated, having lost both his group matches, but he's still playing and he's a competitor.

Then at 8:30 PM CET, Alexander Zverev (2-0, already through) plays Arthur Fils (1-1). Fils is still alive. If Shelton wins, he advances regardless of what happens in the evening match. If Shelton loses, Fils can still reach the last four if the standings fall right.

Zverev playing a "dead rubber" after his work is done could also mean Fils gets a chance to push for a result he needs. That's the tension in tonight's late match.

Who advances from the McEnroe Group alongside Zverev?

stories.title: Medvedev vs Tiafoe Friday — Lendl Group's Second Semifinal Spot

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Friday in Turin: Medvedev (1-1) vs Tiafoe (1-1). Winner takes the last Lendl Group semifinal spot and faces Zverev. Medvedev leads career H2H 4-0. The final group match that actually matters. #ATPFinals #Tennis #ATP #Medvedev

facebook.long_form:
The last group-stage match with genuine stakes at the 2026 ATP Finals is on Friday — Daniil Medvedev against Frances Tiafoe.

Both players are 1-1 in the Ivan Lendl Group. The winner reaches the semifinals. The loser goes home. Carlos Alcaraz is already through as the group winner, so this one truly is a straight shoot-out.

Medvedev leads their career head-to-head record 4-0 — the numbers favour the Russian. But Tiafoe has been building toward this. His first ATP Finals win came on Wednesday, and there is nothing about his game that makes him a pushover indoors. He saved two set points in the tiebreak against Cobolli before dominating the second set, which speaks to resilience under pressure.

The winner faces Zverev in the semifinals on Saturday.

Which player do you back — Medvedev or Tiafoe?

stories.title: Rybakina Closes 2026 as WTA World No. 1

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Elena Rybakina closes 2026 as WTA World No. 1 — the first player representing Kazakhstan to end a year at the top. She is the 17th player in WTA history to achieve it. Andreeva ends at No. 2. #WTA #Tennis #WTARankings #Rybakina

facebook.long_form:
Elena Rybakina ends 2026 at the top of the WTA rankings, cementing a historic year with a distinction no player representing Kazakhstan has held before.

She is the 17th player in WTA history to close a season ranked No. 1 in the world. Rybakina clinched the position on October 29 at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo, finishing the year with 8,099 ranking points. She receives the Chris Evert WTA No. 1 Trophy.

Mirra Andreeva, who won the 2026 WTA Finals in Indian Wells without dropping a set, closes the season at No. 2 with 7,806 points. Iga Swiatek, who held the year-end No. 1 position in 2022, 2023, and 2024, finishes 2026 at No. 9.

It is the kind of season that reshapes how people talk about the sport. Rybakina is at the top of the game.

Who do you think makes the biggest leap in the WTA rankings in 2027?
